readme: Where the gateway's judge of a förläggning (placement-judge.ts judgePlacements) and the web's mirror of it (web/lib/placement-mirror.ts, the ghost under a drag) must agree.
Each case is a small world (`base` plus the case's `add`), one candidate row, and the judge's verdict on it. The verdicts are the REAL judge's, run against a real database
by scripts/test/probe-forlagg-spegel.ts (the adapter probe) and written back here with FORLAGG_SPEGEL_WRITE=1; the web's placement-mirror.contract.test.ts runs the same
worlds through the mirror. The mirror may be STRICTER than the judge and never milder, for the rules it has: where the judge refuses for TEACHER, ROOM, GROUP,
AVAILABILITY, FRAME, LUNCH, GRADE_RULE or SCHOOL_DAY the mirror refuses too. A case with `outsideMirror: true` is a rule the mirror does not have (other schools' bookings,
the post's demand, named pupils): there it is milder by design and the gateway answers at the drop. A case with `mirrorStricter: true` is one where the mirror refuses and the judge does not.
World (names are keys; the database side makes ids of them, the web side uses the keys as ids):
classes   [{key, grade}]                 home classes of the year (grade 4..9)
teachers  [key]                          rooms [key]            subjects [key]
pupils    [{key, class}]                 a pupil's home class

groups    [{key, members: [pupil]}]      teaching groups (kind TEACHING_GROUP, no year of their own), whose members are pupils of the classes: a group shares pupils with every class one of its pupils is in

posts     [{key, class | group, subject, teacher, coTeacher?, minutes, lessons, recurrence?, startDate?, endDate?, minutesBefore?, minutesAfter?, shares?: [{teacher, lessons}], lengths?, block?}]   timplansposter (recurrence defaults to ALL_WEEKS; minutesBefore/After are the pupils' ombyte and dusch around the post's lessons, 0 when left out)
A post is taught to a `class` OR to a teaching `group` (exactly one of them; the web names it studentGroupId). `lengths` (longest first, e.g. [80, 40]) is a post whose lessons are not all one length:
`lessons` is then lengths.length and `minutes` lengths[0]. `block` makes the post a MEMBER of the block of that key (the post's own rows are then refused: a block is laid by its own lesson).
kept      [{class | group, subject, teacher, coTeacher?, room?, day, start, minutes, recurrence?, startDate?, endDate?, extraClasses?: [class], locked?: true}]   lessons Generera keeps
rows      [{post, day, start, minutes, room?, recurrence?, teacher?}]   förläggningar of the posts, already stored (a pinned one has no room)
unavailable [{kind: teacher|room|class|grade, key?, grades?: [min, max], day, start, end}]   UNAVAILABLE constraints (a grade rule names grades, not a key)
frames    [{grades: [min, max], start, end}]                  ramtider for every weekday

meals     [{class, day, start, end, generated?: true}]         lunches the school placed by hand; a `generated` one is a meal Generera laid, which the judge does not hold a row to (and the week's board does not carry)

blocks    [{key, posts: [post key], lessons: [{day, start, minutes, rooms?: {<post key>: <room key>}}]}]   parallel blocks (Språkval): the `posts` are the block's members, and `lessons` the lessons the school has already placed on it, stored as they stand (a lesson that

no longer holds can be stored). A block of the same key in a case's `add` REPLACES the base block (it is not merged). THE MEMBERS agree on lessons, minutes/lengths and recurrence (the database insists), and every member sits every

lesson of the block at once: a lesson of the block is ONE lesson at (day, start, minutes), in the members' weeks (the members' recurrence, and each member post's own startDate/endDate), and each member sits it as its OWN post's

lesson (the member's class or group, subject, teacher, coTeacher, minutesBefore/After). `rooms` names the room a member chose for that lesson (post key -> room key); a member NOT named has its room chosen by the engine: no

room, so no room clash and no room unavailability. A block lesson is one lesson per member for the rules, and the members are held against each other too (different groups stand in nobody's way, but a teacher, a room
or a pupil two members share is a clash).

Candidate, one of two kinds. (a) A POST's row {post, day, start, minutes, room?, recurrence?, teacher?, replaces?} (the judge: the PUT on the post's path; every block of the world, with its stored lessons, is beside it). `replaces` names a `rows`
entry (by index) that the candidate is a move of: the stored row is not beside it (the PUT replaces the whole list), and the mirror must not hold the lesson against its own old place.

(b) A BLOCK's lesson {block, day, start, minutes, rooms?: {<post key>: <room key>}, replaces?} (the judge: PUT /teaching-blocks/:id/placements, with the candidate FIRST in the list, then the block's other stored lessons). `replaces` names a

stored lesson of that block (by index into the world's blocks[block].lessons) that the candidate is a move of: all of that lesson's rows are out of the way of the new place, and ONLY that lesson's: the block's other lessons are not. The

candidate is one lesson of every member of the block, in the block's weeks, with the room each member was given (a member left out of `rooms` has none), and every member's row is held against the week AND against the other members' rows.

Verdict: {ok: true}, or {ok: false, reason} for kind (a), or {ok: false, reason, post} for kind (b): the judge's reasons (placement-judge.ts PlacementRefusalReason), and `post` the first member (in the order of the world's `posts`) whose row is

refused. The mirror must refuse where the judge does and, for kind (b), name that member among those it refuses (it may name more). A stored lesson that is already red is let stand by the judge when the candidate re-states it unchanged
(`replaces` it with the same place and rooms): such a case is `mirrorStricter`, since the mirror holds every lesson against the whole week.
